answer: Yes, you had a scan for a possible blood clot in your lung in July 2025, and it did not find one. A CT angiogram of your chest, done on 8 July 2025, looked for a pulmonary embolism. The report says there was no pulmonary embolism, your lungs were clear, and there was no fluid around the lungs or heart. It also noted mild wear-and-tear changes in the thoracic spine. A blood test (D-dimer) taken the same day was mildly raised. Because the scan was clear, the clot was ruled out, and your records list it as ruled out rather than as a diagnosis. Your records show no later lung clot diagnosis. The records do not say what led to the scan. They list chest wall pain starting 8 July 2025 and resolving by 22 July 2025. Your doctor can tell you more about the cause of that pain.
short: CT chest angiogram on 2025-07-08 showed no pulmonary embolism; D-dimer was mildly raised; the clot was ruled out. No later lung clot in records through 2026-10-15.

items.says: The blood test taken the same day (D-dimer) was mildly raised at 0.92 mg/L, above the reference of 0.49 or less. A raised D-dimer does not by itself mean a clot; imaging is what confirms or rules one out.
items.why: A raised D-dimer is non-specific. The records show the value but do not say why the scan was ordered.
